{{short description|Canadian American mathematician}}
'''Robert Mark Goresky''' is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]] who invented [[intersection homology]] with his advisor and life partner [[Robert MacPherson (mathematician)|Robert MacPherson]].

==Career==
Goresky received his [[Ph.D.]] from [[Brown University]] in 1976.  His thesis, titled ''Geometric Cohomology and Homology of Stratified Objects'', was written under the direction of MacPherson.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=4422}}</ref> Many of the results in his thesis were published in 1981 by the [[American Mathematical Society]]. He has taught at the [[University of British Columbia]] in Vancouver, and [[Northeastern University]].{{cn|date=December 2021}}

==Awards==
Goresky received a Sloan Research Fellowship in 1981.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fellows Database |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database |website=Sloan Foundation |access-date=24 February 2022}}</ref> He received the [[Coxeter–James Prize]] in 1984<ref>{{cite web |url= http://cms.math.ca/Prizes/info/cj.html |website=[[Canadian Mathematical Society]] |title=Coxeter–James Prize |accessdate=3 December 2021}}</ref> and the [[Jeffery-Williams Prize]] in 1996.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cms.math.ca/awards/jeffery-williams-prize/ |website =[[Canadian Mathematical Society]] |title=Jeffery-Williams Prize |accessdate = 25 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://cms.math.ca/wp-content/uploads/awards/citations/jw1996.pdf |website=[[Canadian Mathematical Society]] |title=Award Citations |accessdate=25 August 2025}}</ref> In 2002, Goresky and MacPherson were jointly awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Seminal Contribution to Research by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200204/comm-steeleprz.pdf Notices of the AMS 2002 p. 466]</ref><ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/pabrowse?purl=steele-prize?SCR List of Steele Prizes Seminal Contribution to Research]</ref>
In 2012 Goresky became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref>

== Personal ==
Goresky's PhD advisor, [[Robert MacPherson (mathematician)|Robert D. MacPherson]], later became his life partner. Their discovery of intersection homology made "both of them famous."<ref name=":0" /> After the collapse of the Soviet Union, they were instrumental in channeling aid to Russian mathematicians, especially many who had to hide their sexuality.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2012-05-29 |title=Robert D. MacPherson |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2012/05/30/robert-d-macpherson/ |access-date=2022-05-30 |website=Simons Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* Goresky, Mark; MacPherson, Robert, ''La dualité de Poincaré pour les espaces singuliers'', C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Sér. A-B 284 (1977), no. 24, A1549&ndash;A1551.  {{MathSciNet|id=0440533}}
* Goresky, Mark; MacPherson, Robert,  ''Intersection homology theory'', [[Topology (journal)|Topology]] 19 (1980), no. 2, 135&ndash;162. {{doi|10.1016/0040-9383(80)90003-8}} {{MathSciNet|id=0572580}}
* Goresky, Mark, ''Whitney stratified chains and cochains'', Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 267 (1981), 175&ndash;196.
* Goresky, Mark; MacPherson, Robert, ''Intersection homology. II'', [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] 72 (1983), no. 1, 77&ndash;129. {{doi|10.1007/BF01389130}} {{MathSciNet|id=0696691}}
* Goresky, Mark; MacPherson, Robert, ''Stratified Morse Theory'', Springer Verlag, N. Y. (1989), Ergebnisse vol. 14.
